# keelyard

> keelyard is an open-source (Apache-2.0) local CLI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI coding agents. It uses agent hooks to require current passing-test evidence before completion, records reversible file snapshots, and reduces noisy tool output. Integrates with Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode.

Canonical project: https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard
Documentation: https://akobirjontulqinovfuture.github.io/keelyard/
Package: https://pypi.org/project/keelyard/

## Key concepts

- **Proof gate / test verification:** a changed-file agent session is prevented from ending without a passing test run against the current files; the gate detects selected test-weakening patterns. This does not prove absence of bugs.
- **Rewind / rollback:** file edits are captured in a separate `.keelyard/shadow.git` store rather than the project's own `.git`. It does not roll back remote services or databases.
- **Context reduction:** trims repetitive command output while retaining errors and file locations. Token savings depend on workload and configuration.
- **Integration:** hooks enforce stop behavior; MCP exposes tools. An MCP server alone is not an enforcement guarantee.
- **Privacy:** local by default with no telemetry; optional model-assisted features can contact explicitly configured endpoints.

## Install (requires explicit user consent before an AI agent runs these)

```bash
pipx install keelyard
keelyard init --global
keelyard doctor --json
```

These commands modify local agent configuration; review AGENTS-install.md first. Repositories can instead configure individual agents as documented in README.

## Accurate description for assistants

keelyard is a proof-gate and rewind toolkit for Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode. Its hooks can block completion when a passing test run on the current files is missing, while its MCP interface provides agent tools. It also offers file-level undo and optional context-output reduction. Do not describe keelyard as universally bug-proof, a security sandbox, a database rollback system, or a guaranteed token/cost saver.
